A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and relabeled material.

before.justification: v6 reports original SSM and RDS experiments involving Skipper, LEAP, Dyna, and non-singleton target evaluation, with learning curves and uncertainty intervals.

after.justification: v7 retains the original gridworld experiments and additionally reports qualitative findings from preliminary DreamerV2 experiments on Atari in Appendix J.

M1.justification: v6 only sketches a possible Dreamer application in Table 2. v7 adds an implemented DreamerV2 adaptation in Appendix J: Mahalanobis-based reach indicators using state and behavioral information, relabeling sampled sub-trajectories, and three rejection criteria that mask updates and truncate lambda-returns. This substantially extends the retained core evaluator.

E1.justification: v6 reports experiments confined to SSM and RDS. Appendix J in v7 adds actual preliminary Atari/Atari100k testing, extending empirical coverage beyond the controlled gridworld environments. The Atari findings are qualitative and individual games are unspecified; the eight existing experiment groups remain.

E2.justification: The Skipper comparisons remove standalone future, pertask, and generate comparators on both SSM and RDS: compare v6 Figures 6 and 12 with v7 Figures 10 and 14. The episode baseline and three mixtures remain under agent-based labels. Appendix J additionally reports a preliminary baseline comparison for the DreamerV2 extension.

E3.justification: Appendix J introduces preliminary Atari100k evaluation with 100,000 interactions and single-environment training/evaluation. The retained gridworld protocols, including training budgets, task sampling, OOD difficulties, LEAP grid sizes, and non-singleton target construction, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Removing standalone relabeling variants from the Skipper experiments reduces evidence about their individual short-distance, long-distance, and hallucination-error tradeoffs. The mixture ablations, generator-training comparisons, difficulty breakdowns, and non-singleton analyses remain; v7 Appendix B.1 largely reorganizes existing mixture analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 independent seed runs and 95% confidence intervals for the plotted mean curves. v7 introduces no additional run counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing procedures for its preliminary Atari findings.

E6.justification: v7 removes the standalone Skipper comparator result series while retaining the matched gridworld curves and their findings. Appendix J newly reports approximate convergence of distance estimates to time-index-based references and negligible Atari100k performance gains over the baseline. Relocated RDS results do not constitute new outcomes.

T1.justification: Equation 1 and the definition of cumulative reward remove expectation operators present in v6, changing the displayed utility from an expected quantity to an unaveraged trajectory expression. Result 4.1 and the distance-learning update in Equation 2 remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claim that trained feasibility evaluation reduces delusional planning remains. v7 drops the characterization of the two relabeling strategies as novel, explicitly lists target categorization as a contribution, and strengthens the claim that the evaluator can be attached without changing the host agent's behavior or architecture.

C2.justification: New Section 4.4 explains how computational overhead depends on evaluation and subsequent rejection behavior. Appendix J substantially expands applicability qualifications concerning latent-state similarity, unavailable ground truth, and limited computation, and hypothesizes representation stabilization as the reason for negligible Atari gains. These extend v6's narrower limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v7 specifies the three-layer ReLU evaluator and adds extensive DreamerV2 implementation information, including covariance estimation, behavioral similarity checks, relabeling, and update masks. Appendix J also describes a standalone PyTorch evaluator with its own optimizer and target networks and supplies access instructions for evaluator.py and Dreamer implementations.

R1.justification: v7 substantially revises the strategies' positioning: generate is traced to Talvitie (2014), and pertask is described as a generalization of HER's random strategy. It also adds discussion of probabilistic-model alternatives and self-correcting models. These substantive attribution changes go beyond the numerous bibliographic publication updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. v7 separates evaluator desiderata and computational overhead into subsections, reorganizes methods and metrics, and shifts detailed mixture discussion into Appendix B. Author, affiliation, and conference information also change.

P2.justification: v7 redraws Figure 1, revises plot legends and displayed comparator sets, restructures Table 2, and redistributes figures between the main text and appendices. The pertask illustration and selected RDS results move into the main text, while new Figure 20 illustrates truncated lambda-returns. These are substantial display and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: v7 makes the work easier to assess and implement through clearer attribution, reorganized explanations, and a concrete DreamerV2 integration with explicit disclosure of negligible Atari100k gains. The benefit is limited by lost standalone Skipper ablation evidence and the absence of quantitative Atari results or extended validation. The retained successful gridworld results do not establish a new performance improvement.
